record.paper_title: Lower Bounds for Unrestricted Boolean Circuits: Open Problems
record.original_question: Does there exist a symmetric Boolean function whose circuit size grows superlinearly with n, where symmetric means that the output depends only on the number of 1 bits among the inputs?

evidence.quote: Can one prove a superlinear lower bound for a symmetric function (i.e., a function whose output depends on the sum of input bits only)? In fact, one cannot:
any symmetric function can be computed by a circuit of size 4.5n + o(n) as shown by Demenkov et al. [10].

artifact.self_contained_problem: A Boolean function $f:\{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ is called symmetric if its value depends only on the Hamming weight $|x| = x_1 + x_2 + \cdots + x_n$ of its input. The circuit size $C(f)$ of $f$ is the minimum number of gates in a Boolean circuit over the full binary basis (all two-input Boolean gates allowed) that computes $f$.\n\nQuestion: Does there exist an infinite family $\{f_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ of symmetric Boolean functions $f_n:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ whose circuit size $C(f_n)$ grows superlinearly in $n$, i.e., $C(f_n)/n \to \infty$ as $n\to\infty$?
artifact.status_search_result: It is known that every symmetric Boolean function on n variables can be computed by a Boolean circuit of size at most 4.5n + o(n) (Demenkov, Kojevnikov, Kulikov, Yaroslavtsev), so no symmetric Boolean function family has superlinear circuit complexity. Hence the answer to the question is no.

status_evidence.title: New upper bounds on the Boolean circuit complexity of symmetric functions
status_evidence.snippet: Demenkov, Kojevnikov, Kulikov, Yaroslavtsev show every symmetric Boolean function can be computed by a circuit of size 4.5n+o(n) over the full binary basis.
status_evidence.claim: All symmetric Boolean functions admit linear-size circuits, ruling out superlinear lower bounds.
